text: The template record, its versions and the Legal approval are held in rwb-comms, the merge-field catalog is held in rwb-comms, and the template body file is held in rwb-document with a reference on the template row.
why: Architecture v5 slide 41 and the Ownership Map give templates and merge fields to rwb-comms, which outranks the DL28 answer in the Decision Log, and P5 owns the document store.
read: FSD P6 A2.1 and A2.18 as the template and merge-field product behaviour, with the body file kept by the document hub.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-P6-001; Section 6 FR-P6-001 to FR-P6-005; Section 8.1; Section 9
impact: If the document hub keeps the template catalog instead, CAP-P6-001 loses two tables and this service keeps only the approval record.

text: This service owns the signature-request operation and the e-signature flow; rwb-document stores the signature request, its status and the signed copy, and the treatment records the result through its own contract.
why: Architecture v5 gives signatures to P5 and the Ownership Map resolves the split that way while the API operations stay on P6.
read: FSD P6 A2.8 and A2.9 as this service's flow and the request status as a document-hub record read through its contract.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-P6-009; Section 6 FR-P6-032 to FR-P6-034; Section 8.2; Section 9
confirm: Solution architect with P5, before wave 2
impact: A request status that must be shown on the case screen adds a read to the document hub contract, not a table here.

text: The notice record holds the proof-of-delivery fields (barcode, callback date, delivery status, sent type) and this service applies a returned proof to its notice by barcode, reading the proof rows through rwb-source-data's contract.
why: Architecture v5 makes proof of delivery this service's product, while the functional specification reads the proof from an ACE view; both hold if the proof lands in ACE and is applied here.
read: FSD P6 A2.2 alternate flows as the product behaviour and v_ace_pod as the read path for the proof row.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-P6-005; Section 6 FR-P6-019 to FR-P6-022; Section 8.1, Section 8.2; Section 9
confirm: Solution architect with the ACE team, before wave 2
impact: If ACE holds the proof as its own product, the notice keeps a view of it and CAP-P6-005 shrinks to the state change.

text: REQ-OCC-007 and REQ-OCC-008 are read as this service's contribution to the case record view and the case timeline: the notice and message block with its states and the ordered notice and message history. The view and the timeline are rwb-case's product.
why: Architecture v5 gives the case, its state, queues, timers and timeline to rwb-case, and the ledger that the timeline reads to rwb-source-data.
read: REQ-OCC-007 and REQ-OCC-008 as the content of the block this service serves, not as ownership of the screen.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-P6-010, CAP-P6-011; Section 6 FR-P6-035, FR-P6-036; Section 10
confirm: Product owner with the solution architect, before wave 1 release
impact: If the view is built here, this service needs a screen route on gateway-bff and P3 loses its case screen.

text: A sent message is recorded as an interaction ledger entry owned by rwb-source-data, with its channel, conduct result, delivery status and channel reference, and rwb-comms adds no message table.
why: Architecture v5 gives rwb-comms three objects and gives the interaction ledger to rwb-source-data under the default ruling.
read: FSD P6 A2.3 and A2.4 as the message behaviour and the interaction as the ledger record.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-P6-006; Section 6 FR-P6-023 to FR-P6-026; Section 8.2; Section 9
impact: A message read inside this service adds a read call to the ledger contract on the send path.

text: A send is retried three times on the platform schedule and then placed in the exception queue, and the fifth-attempt wording of the acceptance criteria is kept as source text.
why: NFR-026 and the Arch v5 retry pattern both state three attempts, and the functional specification states five in two criteria.
read: FSD P6 AC-EXC-P6-003-03 and AC-EXC-P6-008-03 with the retry number read as the platform limit.
confirm: Solution architect, before wave 2 system test
impact: A different limit changes one configuration value and the acceptance criterion wording, not the design.

text: JOB-10 (WIN notices, 16:00) is this service's only schedule; the functional specification's reference to JOB-11 for a send retry is read as the platform retry and outbox mechanism.
why: Architecture v5 and the Ownership Map make JOB-11 the outbox relay in every service and give it to the platform.
read: FSD P6 AC-EXC-P6-003-03 and AC-EXC-P6-008-03 as retry behaviour with JOB-11 named as the mechanism that carries it.
impact: A separate retry job would add a schedule and a run book to this service.

text: The WIN registered-mail file layout is a versioned interface definition owned by rwb-integration, and this service writes the file content against that definition and a fake of it.
why: The sources state the file and the fields the notice keeps but not the layout, and v5 makes rwb-integration the owner of outbound files.
read: INT-14 as the interface and the notice fields as the content this service supplies.
applied_in: Section 6 FR-P6-015 to FR-P6-017; Section 9; Section 10
confirm: Solution architect with rwb-integration, before wave 2 system test
impact: A layout that carries fields this service does not hold adds a merge step to the dispatch file.

text: The volume test is sized on the document volume of about 860,000 in 2027 as the upper bound for letters and on the interaction volume for messages, until the business lead states the notice and message counts.
why: No source gives a notice, message or proof volume, and the program's document volume is the closest stated figure.
read: NFR-004 as the upper bound and NFR-001 as the case base.
confirm: Business lead with the data lead, before wave 2 performance test
impact: A materially higher volume changes the dispatch window, not the product behaviour.

text: A retention class is declared on the notice record, the template version and the merge-field catalog as versioned data; the periods stay open under DL26 and rwb-document applies the archive and disposal.
why: NFR-028, NFR-030 and NFR-031 state a class per type with the periods open, and v5 gives retention to rwb-document.
read: FSD P6 A2.21 as the retention behaviour of the case, with the period set by Compliance.
impact: A period shorter than the case's forces the notice record to be kept separately after closure.

text: The contact point, its consent state and its failed count are read and written through rwb-source-data's contract; this service enforces the consent rule, the contact stop and the statutory exception.
why: Architecture v5 and the Ownership Map give contact_point_ext and the extension tables to rwb-source-data.
read: FSD P6 A2.18 as the contact repository behaviour with the data held by the source-data service.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-P6-008, CAP-P6-012; Section 6 FR-P6-029, FR-P6-031, FR-P6-037; Section 9
impact: Every send gains one read call to the source-data contract; a cache with a stated staleness is the only mitigation named here.

text: The Legal approval is recorded on the template version as a decision record written through rwb-decision, and the approval of a demand or recall notice is taken on the generated notice through the approval workflow.
why: REQ-APD-006 makes notices the first use of approval routing while the functional specification also has Legal approving template versions.
read: FSD P6 A2.1 as both approvals and Arch v5 slide 17 (child approval) as the notice approval.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-P6-001, CAP-P6-002; Section 6 FR-P6-002, FR-P6-014; Section 9
confirm: Product owner with Legal counsel, before wave 1 release
impact: If the template approval is routed through the workflow too, the template release waits on an approval task and the catalogue load is slower.

text: The seven features that v5 places elsewhere (payment matching and the plan-payment-missed event, the steering dashboard, partner identities, custody movement, the legal or audit document request and retention on closure) are kept in the source with their identifiers and are not built in this service.
why: Architecture v5 gives each of them a named owner and the R-PREC precedence puts the Arch v5 catalogue first.
read: FSD P6 A2.10 to A2.13 and A2.19 to A2.21 as the source record of behaviour that now belongs to P8, P9, S9 with P4, and P5.
impact: A feature that returns here adds a capability and a table this service does not have.

text: Proof-of-delivery capture stays behind its feature flag until RWB-ACE-001 lands and v_ace_pod exists, and a hand-entered proof against the barcode is the fallback agreed with the litigation business owner.
why: DL43 is open, and v_ace_pod is a Section B view over the ACE additions.
read: FSD P6 A2.2 and its alternate flows as the product behaviour, with the read path dependent on the ACE additions.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-P6-005; Section 6 FR-P6-019; Section 10.4; Section 12
confirm: ACE team lead with the solution architect, before wave 2 release
impact: Without the view, the notice period is counted from the sent date, which the litigation rule R-LIT-09 does not allow.

text: NoticeDelivered is published and rwb-case starts the notice period timer from the callback date; the undelivered path writes the decision record here and calls rwb-case's transfer operation with reason NOTICE_UNSERVED.
why: Timers and transfer belong to rwb-case in v5 and NoticeDelivered is listed as consumed by rwb-case, while no event carries the undelivered path.
read: FSD P6 AC-ALT-P6-001-01 and AC-ALT-P6-001-02 as the two effects, one through an event and one through a call.
confirm: Solution architect with P3, before wave 2
impact: If P3 starts the timer from an event it must read the callback date from the event payload, which adds a field to the event contract.

text: The conduct and consent checks are one versioned rule package governed in rwb-decision and evaluated in rwb-comms with the embedded rule kit, and the conduct and QA officer approves its first version.
why: Architecture v5 gives rule governance to rwb-decision and evaluation to the owning service, and no source names the rule identifiers.
read: FSD P6 A2.5 and A2.6 as the outcome of the rule package, not as a list of rules.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-P6-007; Section 6 FR-P6-027, FR-P6-028; Section 9
confirm: Conduct and QA officer with rwb-decision, before wave 2 release
impact: A conduct rule the package cannot express becomes a service change, so the package is agreed before the build starts.

text: This PRD is issued as Draft with an empty approval table because the business requirements documents it rests on are Draft in this run; the Product Owner and the FDA approve it when they approve the business requirements.
why: No approval is recorded in the business requirements documents of this run, and the run rules make a missing approval an assumption rather than a stop.
read: The empty approval tables of the Program BRD v5 and the Epic 2 BRD v3 as 'not yet approved'.
confirm: Product owner with the FDA, at the requirements approval gate
impact: A change requested at approval is a new version of this document, not an edit of this one.

text: This is version 1 of the PRD P6 family: the folder holds no earlier PRD for this service, and the product baseline is FSD P6 Communications v3 (15 November 2026).
why: Rule R8.2 makes the next version the highest of the family plus one, and no PRD for this service exists before this run.
read: FSD P6 v3 as the product baseline, with its history carried in section 1.3.
confirm: Product owner, at the requirements approval gate
impact: None; a later version supersedes this one in the same folder.

text: Every release date is copied from the Program BRD release plan unchanged and is marked tentative (30 November 2026, 31 December 2026, 28 February 2027, 31 March 2027).
why: User decision U7 and decision DL48 keep the dates unchanged and tentative, and a date is never raised as a gap.
read: Program BRD v5 section 8 and section 10.3 as the release dates of waves 1 to 3.
confirm: Programme manager, at each wave gate
impact: A date change is carried by a new version of this document.
